question_variants: why do customers in one state spend less
how does Texas compare to California
sql:
SELECT u.state,
  COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS buyers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), 2) AS spend_per_buyer,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id), 2) AS aov,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), 2) AS orders_per_buyer
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` AS u ON u.id = oi.user_id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
GROUP BY u.state ORDER BY spend_per_buyer DESC
report: Comparing states on raw revenue only measures population. Normalise per buyer, then decompose: spend_per_buyer = aov x orders_per_buyer. That decomposition is what turns 'they spend less' into either 'they buy cheaper things' or 'they buy less often' — the two require different responses.
